BC_description: In asynchronous flow-control methods such as 'eachOfLimit' (and all similar collection-based methods), 'compose', 'seq', 'waterfall', 'auto', 'autoInject', 'whilst', 'until', and 'forever', calling a step callback with 'false' as the first argument (e.g., callback(false)) will now immediately cancel further iteration and prevent any pending or final callbacks from being called. This breaks prior behavior where such a call was either ignored or treated as a successful step, and the flow would continue or the final callback was always invoked. Code relying on the final callback being triggered—even in cases of cancellation via 'callback(false)'—will no longer work as before. Existing code patterns that expect the final callback to always run, or that rely on error propagation semantics consistent with prior Node.js convention (where 'false' was not interpreted specially), will be disrupted. See PR #1064 and associated references for discussion and rationale.
